My family clocked out by Times Square and we headed to VIV Thai Restaurant & Bar in Hell’s Kitchen. Warm neon, Thai accents, a polished bar vibe—stylish without trying too hard. ✨

What we ordered:
🍤 Yum Sam Grob — Crispy white fish and fish maw tossed with cashews, red onion, and cherry tomatoes; the chili-lime dressing brightens everything—crisp, clean, balanced.

🔥 Tom Yum Goong — Deep, aromatic broth with a tight sweet-sour-heat balance; fresh shrimp and oyster mushrooms. Poured over rice, it just works.

🥢 Moo Ping Nom Sod — Iberico pork skewers with a gentle char; tamarind sauce and crispy garlic lift the savory notes.

🐚 Pad Hoi Gaab — Atlantic razor clams in a savory chili sauce with Thai basil; briny-sweet, springy, and distinctive.

🥚 KAI TOON MOR FAI — Silky steamed-egg hotpot with minced pork, shrimp, and squid; a subtle tang keeps it delicate yet complex.

🥓 MOO GROB TOD PRIK GLEUA — Half-lean, half-fat crispy pork: shattering crackle, garlic-chili perfume, savory finish without the grease.

🍹 Cocktails held their own — the rose-forward drink was a standout—rounded florals with a clean finish; romance in a glass.

Dinner at VIV Thai was more than just a meal—it was an escape from the chaos outside. Every dish felt thoughtfully layered, every flavor well-orchestrated, and the cocktails sealed the evening with elegance. It’s that rare place that feels both elevated and comforting, surprising yet familiar. Walking out, I knew one thing for sure: I’ll be coming back. ✨

V{IV} Thai, located on 49th Street in Midtown Manhattan, truly lives up to its 4.7-star rating and 4,500+ reviews. This isn’t your typical overly sweet Thai food—the flavors here are bold, layered, and seriously impressive.
Highly recommend their signature Leng Nam Ngeow, a slow-braised pork rib soup that’s rich and deeply flavorful. The Kai Toon Mor Fai—a steamed egg served in a mini hot pot—is silky smooth and super comforting. Muk Kai Khem, the salted egg yolk squid, is crispy, savory, and addictive. Pad Hoi Gaab, the Thai-style clams, are fresh and tossed in a fragrant, slightly spicy sauce.
For starters, the Peek Gai Yud Sai Oua—boneless wings stuffed with Chiang Mai sausage—is packed with flavor and a great way to kick off the meal.
Don’t miss the jasmine crab fried rice. The portion is generous, loaded with real crab meat—perfect for sharing among four. It’s fragrant, well-seasoned, and could easily stand on its own.
Their cocktails are tropical, colorful, and refreshing—perfect for summer. With most dishes priced in the $20 range, this place is an incredible value for the quality. A must-visit for any Thai food lover.

Most pieces I’ve created in the studio in the last few years have featured mesh spandex, a material I source directly from the garment district here in New York. I use this material in various ways but often it’s layered or sewn into the surface of a piece as a see-thru element—a semi-opaque material collaged over others akin to a glaze of oil paint or an even spatter of spray paint. Other materials I stumble upon in the wild while out walking the streets and commuting around the city. The focal of this piece however, is a collection of protective gloves that I’ve amassed (and used) from various work sites and gigs, severed and augmented into a fractured rectangle. Swaths of burlap are also present, partially exposed and raw or hidden by thick, flat layers of paint. I’m referencing the city and my relationship to its’ niche subcultures, but also talking about labor, the work that drives industry forward; reality.

Not on my end.

I’m not affordable - and I don’t try to be.
Not because I’m difficult.
Because I care too much.

Only I know how much love, time, pressure, and obsession goes into every single shoot.
The hours before.
The hours after.
The thinking. The fixing. The re-editing. The not-sleeping.

Yes, I’ve lowered my price before - when I saw real excitement, respect, and trust in my vision.
That’s different.

But if someone downgrades my work just because they can’t afford it?
That’s fine. Truly.
There are many photographers you can book.

I don’t want everyone.
I don’t need volume.
I physically don’t have time for that - I literally schedule when I breathe and sometimes forget to eat.

I work on quality, not quantity.
On people who take pride in creating something meaningful with me.
On clients who value vision, not discounts.

My prices are non-negotiable because my standards are.

When you are next in Union Square, take a “minuto” out of your day for a dessert that is definitely worth the pay.

Here at one of my favorite restaurants, KYU in Wynwood, with My Forever Soulmate! Here we are celebrating our July 4th Wedding Anniversary and kicking off my Pre-July 5th Birthday Celebration — though You All Know I Celebrated All Month Long, so this is just the first Spark that LIGHT’S IT UP ⚡️🧨🎇✨❤️🎉

We started with the Roasted Cauliflower — tender and charred just right, with creamy goat cheese and a shishito-herb vinaigrette that cut through and cleansed the palate.

Then came the Pork Belly Bao Buns — soft, pillowy clouds wrapped around melt-in-your-mouth pork belly, balanced with just the right amount of pickles and sauce. Each bite was that perfect combo of sweet, salty, and savory — the kind of bite you close your eyes for.😋

Next up, the Smoked Bone Marrow, rich and unctuous, paired with shiso chimichurri and miso toast — each bite a little ritual of indulgence. Then the Mussels in XO sauce, spiced up, brought the briny taste of the sea with a spicy kick that warmed you from the inside out. Vibrant, Tasty & Beautifully Presented.

But the Star that steals my ❤️ is Always the Thai Rice Stone Pot with Duck. The duck — succulent and savory — nestled in fragrant rice, steam rising, flavors all melded together. Then a fried egg on top, glistening yolk ready to break. Stirred at the table so that each grain of rice, each slice of duck, and the runny egg yolk become one harmonious mouthful. Comforting, bold, and Oh-So-Satisfying.

Sharing my Foodie Adventure with My Love — tasting our Faves, feeding each other little bites, laughing over sauces, pausing to just absorb the moment — that’s what makes it transcend a meal. Reminiscing & Sharing how We Met… It was So Unexpected But OHHH So Special…It’s Part of Our Story, Our Happily Ever After — Always a Long Weekend Celebration of Love- Forever Wrapped in Delicious Memories of Us💕

Here’s to many More Dates, many More Days & Nights, Like this, and many More Years! Celebrating Our Life & Love in Full Color. 🥂❤️

O KYU (@kyurestaurants) localizado em Wynwood, é um restaurante que combina ambiente moderno e descolado com uma proposta culinária criativa de inspiração asiática feita na grelha a lenha.
O menu segue o conceito “wood-fired Asian inspired” e a ideia são pratos para compartilhar. Entre os pratos mais pedidos, destacam-se o crispy tuna tartare, a couve-flor assada com queijo de cabra, o frango frito coreano crocante, além do short rib defumado. As guarnições, como o Thai fried rice ou o stone pot, completam bem a refeição, enquanto a sobremesa mais famosa é o coconut cake.
A carta de drinks acompanha a proposta, com opções de coquetéis autorais e clássicos. O serviço é ágil e atencioso.
Seu ambiente tem um ar industrial, com madeira, concreto aparente e cozinha aberta que deixa à vista o fogo e a movimentação dos chefs — ideal para grupos ou para quem busca uma experiência gastronômica mais descontraída. Obs: pode ser um pouco barulhento, o que não favorece encontros intimistas, mas é perfeito para quem busca uma noite animada com comida boa.

Celebrates Publication of Her New Book, ‘MarieBelle Entertains’ 

PHOTOGRAPHED by VITAL AGIBALOW for HENSEL 

MarieBelle New York’s flagship store at 484 Broome Street was the setting for an exquisite evening as Maribel Lieberman, chocolatier, entrepreneur, and author, celebrated the success of her latest book,Maribelle Entertains. 
 
Guests gathered in the heart of SoHo to meet Lieberman, who personally signed copies of her book while sharing her passion for entertaining with elegance and creativity. Maribelle Entertains offers a glimpse into Lieberman’s world of gracious hospitality, featuring curated tablescapes, decadent menus, and heartfelt hosting tips inspired by her global travels and culinary expertise.
 
Attendees indulged in MarieBelle’s signature artisanal chocolates and gourmet treats while enjoying an intimate atmosphere that reflected Lieberman’s refined aesthetic. The event brought together influencers, tastemakers, and devoted fans eager to celebrate the art of entertaining and the beauty of bringing people together.
 
Lieberman expressed gratitude for the overwhelming support, stating, “This book is a love letter to the joy of hosting and creating unforgettable moments. I’m thrilled to share it in such a special space surrounded by friends and kindred spirits.”
 
For those who missed the event, Maribelle Entertains by Rizzoli Books is available for purchase at MarieBelle New York’s flagship store and online.
 
Notable attendees included: Maribel Lieberman, Sean Young, and Nicole Miller.
